mcqs.question: What does this review call the standard of care for a potentially resectable Pancoast tumor?

options.A: Induction chemoradiotherapy followed by an attempt at complete resection
options.B: Surgery alone with no preoperative treatment
options.C: Chemotherapy without any plan for resection

mcqs.correctAnswerText: Induction chemoradiotherapy followed by an attempt at complete resection
mcqs.explanation: Induction chemoradiotherapy is the standard of care for any potentially resectable Pancoast tumor, followed by an attempt at complete resection.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Induction chemo-radiotherapy is the standard of care for any potentially resectable Pancoast tumor followed by an attempt to achieve a complete tumor resection.

mcqs.question: Which features does the review include in the Pancoast-Tobias syndrome?

options.A: Horner syndrome, severe shoulder pain, muscle atrophy, and subclavian vein obstruction
options.B: Only a cough with a normal shoulder exam

mcqs.correctAnswerText: Horner syndrome, severe shoulder pain, muscle atrophy, and subclavian vein obstruction
mcqs.explanation: The syndrome includes Claude-Bernard-Horner syndrome, severe shoulder pain, atrophy of hand and arm muscles, and obstruction of the subclavian vein.

sourceRefs.excerpt: clinically evident with the characteristic symptoms of the “Pancoast-Tobias syndrome” which includes Claude-Bernard-Horner syndrome, severe pain in the shoulder radiating toward the axilla and/or scapula and along the ulnar distribution of the upper arm, atrophy of hand and arm muscles and obstruction of the subclavian vein resulting in edema of the upper arm.

mcqs.question: What 5-year survival does the review give for R0 resection?

options.E: The same as unresectable disease in this sentence

mcqs.explanation: The review says 5-year survival for R0 resections is quite good, 54 to 77 percent. Complete resection rates in the same passage vary from 55 to 70 percent.

sourceRefs.excerpt: the 5-year survival for R0 resections is quite good (54-77%).

mcqs.question: Which inlet structures does the review say these tumors can involve?

options.A: The lower brachial plexus, the stellate ganglion, and the subclavian vessels, among others

mcqs.correctAnswerText: The lower brachial plexus, the stellate ganglion, and the subclavian vessels, among others
mcqs.explanation: The review lists the lower nerve roots of the brachial plexus, the upper sympathetic chain and stellate ganglion, and the subclavian vein and artery.

sourceRefs.excerpt: lower nerve roots of the brachial plexus, the upper sympathetic chain and stellate ganglion, the subclavian vein and artery), producing that way a special clinical picture that is well known in the medical literature as the Pancoast-Tobias or Pancoast syndrome (1-6).

mcqs.question: What does the review call the main pattern of recurrence?

options.A: Distant metastases, especially in the brain
options.C: Recurrence does not occur after R0 resection

mcqs.correctAnswerText: Distant metastases, especially in the brain
mcqs.explanation: The main pattern of recurrence is distant metastases, especially in the brain.

sourceRefs.excerpt: The main pattern of recurrence is that of distant metastases, especially in the brain.
